ava.name: af_bella
ava.note: Tessa, the ONLY voice of the four Instagram reels (the client: the woman's voice speaks whenever there is text on screen). She is the narrator (untagged captions) and the sample agent Ava on the calls (captions tagged ● AVA). Callers are never voiced: ig2 and ig3 are one-sided calls (the agent restates what was asked; the caller's turn is a slate level meter with no words), ig4's phrasings are read by the narrator under the site's own 'Asked as' label. Full-band, no phone line. Same voice id and speed as film 2's ava role.

lines.say: Don't pay three hundred a month for an AI receptionist.
lines.direction: Reel 5 hook, narrator, from frame 0 over the desk phone's ring and a blank quote slip: calm and dry, one owner warning another, not an ad (the shape of ig1-01 "Don't fire your receptionist for an AI."). Light stress on "three hundred", heard by about 1.2 s; no pause after "month"; "AI receptionist" said plainly (it is the TikTok search phrase). Captions show $300 over "three hundred". Target 3.6 s or less.
lines.speak: Don't pay three hundred a month for an AI receptionist.

lines.say: That's a common agency retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.
lines.direction: Reel 5, narrator, reading an agency quote back: matter-of-fact, never mocking. A small natural beat at the full stop. "often" gets honest weight (it is the hedge and must be heard); "fifteen hundred" a touch slower. Captions show $1,500. as the display of "fifteen hundred."
lines.speak: That's a common agency retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.

lines.say: Live answering service: from ninety-nine a month, for fifty minutes.
lines.direction: Reel 5, narrator: even and factual, with no judgement of the people who answer. "Live" and "from" audible; "for fifty minutes" clear, because it is the qualifier that makes $99 true. Captions show $99 and 50.
lines.speak: Live answering service: from ninety-nine a month, for fifty minutes.

lines.say: Ours? From forty-nine dollars a month. No setup fee.
lines.direction: Reel 5 PAYOFF, narrator, spoken out of the stop-time silence right after the phone is picked up: a small, real lift on "Ours?", then warm and settled, unhurried on "forty-nine dollars a month" ("From" light but present: it is the hedge). "No setup fee" plain. Word SII on "forty-nine dollars" must reach 0.7 (captions show $49). No <break/>: Sonic already pauses at the question mark and the full stops.
lines.speak: Ours? From forty-nine dollars a month. No setup fee.

lines.say: You set it up yourself, in under ten minutes.
lines.direction: Reel 5, narrator, as four dots fill teal: easy and encouraging, a fact, not a boast (the site's own "Ready in under ten minutes"). "yourself" carries the basis of the comparison (an agency builds it for you; this you do yourself); "under" clearly said. Never "five minutes".
lines.speak: You set it up yourself, in under ten minutes.

lines.say: It picks up when you can't, and books the appointment.
lines.direction: Reel 5, narrator, over the sample call record: warm and assured. "when you can't" gentle (it is the viewer's problem, and ig1's position: the desk keeps its people). "books the appointment" is the satisfying close. LAUNCH-GATED: placed in the booking master; ig5-06-msg is placed in the message master, and both masters are rendered (POSTING §0). The booking master is posted only once booking works on the $49 Starter plan.
lines.speak: It picks up when you can't, and books the appointment.

lines.direction: Reel 5 CTA, narrator, the same words as ig2-07 but a fresh ig5 take (PIPELINE allows exactly one borrow, ig1-07): confident, slightly lower and warm. No "free" in this reel's CTA (booking is on screen; the captions and DM carry the trial). speak has "agent" in lowercase so Sonic does not spell it out.

lines.say: A common agency retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.
lines.direction: TRIM T1 for ig5-02 (one token shorter), picked by timing.ts only if the measured takes would push the CTA past f765. Same read as ig5-02. Screens become S3 [0-3] "A common agency retainer." and S4 [4-7] "Setup, often $1,500." (display [6-7]).
lines.speak: A common agency retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.

lines.direction: TRIM T2 for ig5-05 (four tokens shorter, about 1.4 s), used together with T1 only if the takes still run long. Same read, a touch more settled at the end since it closes the beat. One card; "in under ten minutes" stays in both captions.

lines.say: It picks up when you can't, and takes a message.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig5-06, THE NO-BOOKING CUT: true on Starter today (take_message). Use it if the owner's Starter booking change is not live on posting day; the record then shows "Took a message" and the indigo Message taken pill. Same read and length as ig5-06.
lines.speak: It picks up when you can't, and takes a message.

lines.say: Before you pay three hundred a month for an AI receptionist.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE HOOK (A/B, hookscore 87.0) for a second TikTok post a week later or a Trial Reel once the account has about 200 followers: same calm, dry read as ig5-01, addressed to someone about to sign. Cards: "Before you pay $300 a month" / "for an AI receptionist." It flows into ig5-02 unchanged.
lines.speak: Before you pay three hundred a month for an AI receptionist.

lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig5-07, only if nobody can answer AGENT comments (and the Instagram comment-to-DM automation is not live) on posting day: same read, same slot.

lines.say: Plus the number: a dollar fifteen a month.
lines.direction: SPARE, not placed by default: if the owner wants the phone-number cost spoken instead of the setup line, it replaces ig5-05 (time-neutral). Light and candid, the small print said out loud with a half-smile and no apology; "a dollar fifteen" clear (captions show $1.15).
lines.speak: Plus the number: a dollar fifteen a month.

lines.say: Three rings. Gloves on. You can't.
lines.direction: Reel 5 HOOK (docs/ig/ig5/HOOKS.md §1, the TikTok tournament winner), narrator, over the desk phone's third ring in a quiet room (no music yet): an owner naming a moment, not an ad. Calm, close and dry: three short falling sentences, gaps of 0.25 s or less. No drama on "can't", but its t must be released: a read that sounds like "can" inverts the line and is rejected. Card S1 [0-5] set at frame 0: "Three rings." / "Gloves on." / "You can't." ("Three" stays a word). Target about 2.1-2.4 s.
lines.speak: Three rings. Gloves on. You can't.

lines.say: Three rings, gloves on. You can't.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE READING of ig5-01g (HOOKS §1.1), about 0.3 s quicker: two breaths instead of three, the same calm, dry read; "can't" with its t released. The same card: the display map shows "rings," as "rings." and "gloves" as "Gloves". timing.ts places it only if ig5-01g would put "Agency AI receptionist:" on screen after f78 (HOOKS §1.1 cast rule).
lines.speak: Three rings, gloves on. You can't.

lines.say: Agency AI receptionist: three hundred a month, a common retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.
lines.direction: Reel 5 beat 2 for the winning hook (HOOKS §1.6, replaces ig5-02): read it like the price list it is, the same shape as ig5-03 ("Live answering service: ..."), matter-of-fact, never mocking. A small beat after the label. Light stress on "three hundred" and on "often" (the hedge: it must be heard); "common" audible; "fifteen hundred" a touch slower. Cards S2 [0-2] "Agency AI receptionist:" / S3 [3-9] "$300 a month, a common retainer." / S4 [10-13] "Setup, often $1,500."
lines.speak: Agency AI receptionist: three hundred a month, a common retainer. Setup, often fifteen hundred.

lines.say: Agency AI receptionist: commonly three hundred a month. Setup, often fifteen hundred.
lines.direction: TRIM T1 for ig5-02g (HOOKS §1.1, two tokens shorter), placed by timing.ts only if the full cast would push the CTA past f765. Same read as ig5-02g; "commonly" keeps the hedge and must be heard. Cards S2 [0-2] / S3 [3-7] "commonly $300 a month." / S4 [8-11] "Setup, often $1,500."
lines.speak: Agency AI receptionist: commonly three hundred a month. Setup, often fifteen hundred.

lines.direction: RUNNER-UP HOOK for a later TikTok A/B (HOOKS §2, callout-3; its ig5-01n), over a phone ringing in a closed shop: a small rise on "nine?", then a dry, falling "not."
